proposal.title: Zororvquel: a bandwidth measurement tool for relays
proposal.summary: Zororvquel builds a bandwidth measurement tool for relays for volunteer relay operators.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.text: Relay operators cannot tell whether their relay serves traffic well. Volunteer relay operators depend on onion routing every day, yet the tools they have are hard to audit and slow to update.

sections.heading: Approach
sections.text: We will build a bandwidth measurement tool for relays called Zororvquel. The work starts from a written threat model and ends with a reproducible release. Each component gets tests and a fuzz target before it is merged.

sections.heading: Relevance to the Open Internet Stack
sections.text: Onion routing is part of the Open Internet Stack. An open implementation lets anyone inspect, reuse and improve it without asking a vendor for permission.

sections.heading: Team and experience
sections.text: We maintain http://forge.test/zororvquel/zororvquel, which 43 public projects depend on. Our team has worked on onion routing for 8 years.

sections.heading: Deliverables and licence
sections.text: All code will be released under the Apache-2.0 licence in http://forge.test/zororvquel/zororvquel. Documentation will be published under CC BY 4.0.

sections.heading: Milestones
sections.text: The work runs over 9 months in 4 milestones. Design and threat model ends in month 2. Core implementation ends in month 4. Testing and fuzzing ends in month 7. Documentation and release ends in month 9.

sections.heading: Budget justification
sections.text: The plan asks for 71400.00 EUR for 107 days of work over 4 tasks. Day rates range from 500.00 EUR to 750.00 EUR.

proposal.narrative:
Problem
Relay operators cannot tell whether their relay serves traffic well. Volunteer relay operators depend on onion routing every day, yet the tools they have are hard to audit and slow to update.

Approach
We will build a bandwidth measurement tool for relays called Zororvquel. The work starts from a written threat model and ends with a reproducible release. Each component gets tests and a fuzz target before it is merged.

Relevance to the Open Internet Stack
Onion routing is part of the Open Internet Stack. An open implementation lets anyone inspect, reuse and improve it without asking a vendor for permission.

Team and experience
We maintain http://forge.test/zororvquel/zororvquel, which 43 public projects depend on. Our team has worked on onion routing for 8 years.

Deliverables and licence
All code will be released under the Apache-2.0 licence in http://forge.test/zororvquel/zororvquel. Documentation will be published under CC BY 4.0.

Milestones
The work runs over 9 months in 4 milestones. Design and threat model ends in month 2. Core implementation ends in month 4. Testing and fuzzing ends in month 7. Documentation and release ends in month 9.

Budget justification
The plan asks for 71400.00 EUR for 107 days of work over 4 tasks. Day rates range from 500.00 EUR to 750.00 EUR.
